questions.q: Why was David eager to speak privately with Neil Roy Macrob, the ferry skipper?
choices: Macrob was a name of Alan's clan, and Alan had sent him there
Neil Roy was said to be the best guide in all of Morven
Neil Roy had been a sailor on the brig Covenant before
David wanted to ask him for work on the ferry-boat
questions.evidence: since Macrob was one of the names of Alan's clansmen

questions.q: Why was the ferry crossing so slow?
choices: A storm kept pushing the boat back toward Mull
There was no wind and the boat could pull only three oars
The skipper kept stopping to talk to other boats
The boat was so crowded that water kept coming in over the side
questions.evidence: we could pull but two oars on one side, and one on the other

questions.q: What was the big ship anchored in the mouth of Loch Aline?
choices: One of the King's cruisers watching the coast
An emigrant ship bound for the American colonies
A French ship that had come to carry away Jacobites
A fishing ship bringing herring to the market
questions.evidence: this was an emigrant ship bound for the American colonies

questions.q: Why were the people on the ship and on the beach crying and lamenting?
choices: A storm had sunk one of the skiffs
Friends and families were being parted for good
The ship's captain would not let them come aboard
They had heard that Ardshiel had died in France
questions.evidence: the exiles leaned over the bulwarks, weeping and reaching out their hands

questions.q: What was the name of the sad song sung as the ferry pulled away from the emigrant ship?
choices: "Lochaber no more"
"The Bonnie Banks of Loch Aline"
"Farewell to the Heather"
"The Road to Appin"
questions.evidence: which is one called "Lochaber no more"

questions.q: Why was Neil Roy offended when David first asked him about Alan?
choices: David called him by the wrong clan name
David tried to hand him a shilling
David asked him in front of a crowd of Macleans
David said Alan was a rebel and a deserter
questions.evidence: I sought to pass a shilling in his hand

questions.q: What did David do after Neil Roy claimed that Alan was in France?
choices: He offered Neil a whole guinea instead
He showed him the silver button in his palm
He gave up and asked the way to Torosay
He told Neil the whole story of the fight in the round-house
questions.evidence: showed him the button lying in the hollow of my palm

questions.q: Where was the last place on the route Neil Roy gave David?
choices: The house of James of the Glens, at Aucharn in Duror of Appin
The house of John of the Claymore, in the country of Ardgour
The public inn at Kinlochaline, near the shore of Loch Aline
The ferry at Corran, where Alan would be waiting with a boat
questions.evidence: ask my way to the house of James of the Glens, at Aucharn in Duror of Appin

questions.q: What did Neil tell David to do if he saw red-soldiers coming?
choices: Walk on boldly and greet them in English
Leave the road and lie in a bush
Show them Alan's silver button
Run to the nearest Stewart house
questions.evidence: to leave the road and lie in a bush if I saw any of the latter coming

questions.q: What happened at the inn at Kinlochaline during the thunderstorm?
choices: Lightning set the turf roof on fire
One end of the house became running water
The innkeeper locked David out in the rain
The storm blew the door off its hinges
questions.evidence: one end of the house became a running water

questions.q: What bond did David and Mr. Henderland discover they shared?
choices: They had both been kidnapped and sold at sea
Henderland used Gaelic books translated by David's minister
Henderland had known David's father as a schoolboy
They were both on their way to see James of the Glens
questions.evidence: had translated into the Gaelic in his by-time a number of hymns and pious books which Henderland used

questions.q: Why did David tell Henderland he was going to Balachulish instead of Aucharn?
choices: He had changed his plans after the storm
He did not want to lead anyone to Alan's friends
Henderland had warned him that Aucharn was unsafe
He had forgotten the name of the place Neil told him
questions.evidence: might put him on the scent

questions.q: Henderland calls Alan Breck "a fair heather-cat" who is "here to-day and gone to-morrow." What does he mean?
choices: That Alan is wild and hard to catch
That Alan keeps a pet cat in the hills
That Alan is gentle and friendly
That Alan is lazy and sleeps all day
questions.evidence: He's here and awa; here to-day and gone to-morrow: a fair heather-cat

questions.q: What question did Henderland keep asking David over and over?
choices: Whether he had any money to spare
Whether he carried any snuff
Whether he had ever met Alan Breck
Whether he could read the Gaelic
questions.evidence: Ye'll no carry such a thing as snuff, will ye?

questions.q: According to Henderland, where were the first tenants to be turned out the next day?
choices: At Duror, right under James's windows
At Mamore, in the country of the Camerons
At Kingairloch, near Henderland's own house
At Torosay, on the far side of the Sound
questions.evidence: It's to begin at Duror under James's very windows

questions.q: What did Henderland believe might happen to Colin Campbell?
choices: He would be made a lord by the King for his work
He would get his death from Appin or Mamore
He would give up and go back to Edinburgh
He would make peace with James of the Glens
questions.evidence: if he escapes the one lot, he'll get his death by the other

questions.q: Why did Henderland rush in and take huge pinches of snuff the moment he got home?
choices: He had a cold and needed to clear his nose
He had vowed never to carry snuff, so he craved it
He wanted to hide it before David could take some
He was showing David a Highland custom of welcome
questions.evidence: I took a vow upon me that I wouldnae carry it

questions.q: What does David learn about Mr. Henderland by the end of the chapter?
choices: That he is a spy for Colin Campbell
That he is a truly good and humble man
That he is a cheat like the guide on Mull
That he is secretly one of Alan's clan
